title: Shots Madison and playing second trumpet by ear
summary: Asked for last thoughts, Ernie praises Shots Madison as a gifted second trumpet. He explains that playing second by ear was common, as with King Oliver and Louis Armstrong, and the tape runs out.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing the interview: thanks, goodbyes and tape running out

blocks.x: About one more minute left here. About another minute left on the tape. Is there anything else you want to say before we quit? About, uh, either any of the jobs you've played. Or any of your favorite musicians. Or anything at all that you want to add to the story. I know that you have Shots Madison down there.
Yeah, well, he's one of them I put on that I played several jobs with him. Did you play parades and things too? Yeah, I played parades with Shots. Shots.
He was supposed to be pretty good, wasn't he?
He was more, more, a second trumpet player. Good second. He really could fill in on second. He's really had the year for that.
Is the second a little more difficult to play, second trumpet?

Well, I mean, especially when you're not reading the music, you understand? It's an off harmony, see? And quite naturally, if you don't have the year, it's just like if you try to sing a song and I'm trying to do the alto part behind you or the tenor part, I don't have the music in front of me. Well, he's got that from memory and feeling on his fingers. And he was perfect at it. He did, you know. Matter of fact, that's what Lewis stated in that last book. I read it with him and all the people in Chicago when he first went up there. It was baffling the way he and King Oliver did that together so great and they didn't see no music in front of them. Couldn't understand how they did it, you know. Playing duets like they did and no music in front of them. That was a common thing down here?
It always has been. I mean, we do it right now in parades and funerals. Look how more you do right here is playing the man in parades.

I don't need no music to play no second behind Alba Fernandez or one of them. He don't need no music to play no second behind me on his alto. He's training his guys already. He's been doing it so long.
That looks like that's about it. It's about two seconds.
